topics.title: Capability map
topics.summary: Explore an immutable model, query exact sparse relations, verify claims, and build another snapshot.
topics.guarantees: Help only retrieves installed documentation; it does not analyze or change a model.
topics.non_guarantees: IR roles and graph candidates are not mathematical proofs.
topics.body:
Explore: m.ir; m.rows; m.vars; m.terms().
Relate: Frame.where/select/join/group_by; VarFrame.project.
Compare: mf.ops.sets, mf.ops.graph, mf.ops.equal_groups.
Compute: m.matrix.nnz/activity/transpose_activity; sparse MatrixView.
Search: mf.alg.graph and mf.alg.integer; distinguish candidates from exhaustive results.
Verify: LinExpr, Claim, m.check, Report.
Modify: m.edit(), build(), diff(), native save, exact LP audit.

Start with mf.help("coordinates"), mf.help("support containment"),
mf.help("linear certificate"), or mf.help("edit model").
Use detail="full" on a topic ID to read its complete instructions.
Use mf.help("skill", detail="full") for the portable onboarding guide.

topics.title: Rows, variables and sparse terms
topics.summary: Rows and Vars are entity sets; Terms are original nonzero (row, var, coef) relationships.
keywords: coefficient adjacency neighbor sparse schema key
topics.inputs: A live Model. Rows: row,name,lb,ub. Vars: var,name,kind,lb,ub,obj. Terms: row,var,coef.
topics.guarantees: Row/Var IDs are typed, snapshot-qualified identities; names are display and explicit lookup data.
topics.non_guarantees: An entity neighborhood does not retain one edge per source. A Row or Var has no coef field.
topics.example:
r = m.rows.iloc[0]
x = m.vars.by_name("x")
T = x.terms
edge = T.head(1).one()
edge.row, edge.var, edge.coef
topics.body:
Use r.vars and x.rows for deduplicated neighborhoods; use r.terms, x.terms or m.terms(rows=R, vars=V) for coefficients.
Use .iloc for positions, .loc for declared keys, .by_name for names and m.family(label).rows or .vars for family members.
RowFrame.loc and VarFrame.loc accept integer IDs or same-snapshot, same-axis Refs within the selection.
select/join return ordinary Frames. where/head/sort preserve entity type. Entity sets support &, | and -.
Ref columns retain their snapshot and axis. .refs("var") returns the corresponding entity set.
Terms group-by observes only present groups. m.matrix.nnz retains zero-degree members.
select does not invent uniqueness for a projected non-key. joins enforce their declared cardinality before yielding even head(1).

topics.title: Snapshot identity and lifecycle
topics.summary: Independent imports have independent identities; native save/load retains uid and content version.
topics.guarantees: Alignment uses uid, version, entity axis and ID. Canonical kind is C/I; binary is derived from integer bounds.
topics.non_guarantees: Names do not establish an original-to-presolved mapping. Exact saved values do not preserve unsaved source tokens.
topics.body:
Model is immutable. Keep all models referenced by a query open while using live results or suspended iterators.
Exported records contain detached Ref identity values. Bind them explicitly to the matching snapshot to navigate entities.
Use m.rows.loc[ref] or m.vars.loc[ref] for same-snapshot, same-axis references; selections still enforce membership.
ref.bind(m) uses the full matching model. loc[ref.id] discards the Ref snapshot and axis checks.
Same uid with conflicting versions is rejected. New Edit snapshots have new uid and explicit parent/lineage.
read/load prepare default IR and indexed results synchronously. Help and repr do not start an additional discovery run.
Only native v3 is accepted; reimport LP/MPS for older native formats.

topics.title: Claims, reports and proof scope
topics.summary: A Claim states a proposition; only the matching completed checker establishes its stated conclusion.
topics.guarantees: Report status is PROVED, REFUTED or INCONCLUSIVE. require() succeeds only for PROVED.
topics.non_guarantees: Structural checks, feasible points, solver status and graph candidates cannot serve as linear proofs.
topics.body:
identity compares algebra, linear checks supplied multipliers, infeasible checks a contradiction, round uses model integrality,
enumerate checks a finite local integer domain, and solution checks a complete point against the mathematical integer model, including integrality.
For a fractional LP point, use matrix.activity plus exact comparisons of both row sides and all variable bounds, with complete variable coverage.
solution rejects domain="relaxation". linear_many batches explicit certificates.
These checkers do not search for multipliers or solve the MIP. A failed certificate is INCONCLUSIVE, not a proof of the opposite claim.
Assumptions propagate and remain conditional. A local enumeration counterexample need not extend to a feasible point of the full model.
Relaxation-valid evidence can support integer claims, but integer-only evidence cannot establish a relaxation claim.
Use original row/variable side claims, not a newly typed unproved equivalent Claim, as trusted sources.
Proof replay rechecks sources and dependencies; a saved PROVED string carries no authority.

topics.title: Conditions and explicit finite case discharge
topics.summary: Ordinary checkers retain assumptions; check.cases explicitly discharges exhaustive finite integer branches.
keywords: conditional branches case analysis split binary switch merge proofs
topics.guarantees: A conditional report records every explicit and inherited assumption.
topics.non_guarantees: Contradiction under z=1 is not automatically converted to an unconditional z=0 Report usable by Edit. Continuous disjunctions and infeasible-branch elimination are unsupported.
topics.body:
General linear assumptions require explicit multipliers. Assumptions are not searched or silently removed.
When possible, form an unconditional linear bound from original row sides, compensate the residual with bounds, then round an integer expression.
For a finite model-integer variable y, check.cases(target, var=y, cases={0:p0,1:p1}) checks exhaustive coverage and removes only the matching y=value assumptions.
Every branch must prove the same exact target. Other explicit and inherited assumptions remain as a union, so only an empty residual assumption set gives unconditional evidence.
Coverage uses ceil(model lb)..floor(model ub), not assumption-tightened bounds. The result is integer-only, even when all branches are relaxation-valid.

topics.title: Tighten a big-M bound with explicit certificates
topics.summary: Derive a candidate bound from original row sides, then verify the proposed gated inequality.
keywords: big M bigM tightening strengthen indicator gated constraint bound
topics.inputs: An explicit gated row, switch domain, candidate M and original source sides.
topics.guarantees: check.linear verifies supplied unconditional combinations; check.enumerate can verify a finite pure-integer local implication.
topics.non_guarantees: No automatic big-M optimizer or general branch-proof merger is provided. A resource bound alone need not imply the gated inequality.
topics.body:
Use check.linear(target, using=..., residual="bounds") for an explicit unconditional certificate.
A bound s<=U does not by itself prove s<=U*z. Account for the switch and both branches.
check.infeasible or check.linear with assume=[z.eq(0)] or assume=[z.eq(1)] retains the assumption.
Use check.cases(target, var=z, cases={0:p0,1:p1}) to discharge both branches of a model binary; other assumptions remain.
check.enumerate only accepts a finite integer domain after substitutions; it cannot enumerate continuous activity variables.
For row replacement, first add the proved new row and build, then prove the old row from retained facts on that new snapshot and delete it. Diff compares direct parent snapshots only.
Only a supported unconditional proof can justify Edit.add_row(..., because=proof).

topics.title: Set covers and resource bounds
topics.summary: Inspect coverage using set relations; verify a chosen resource-row combination with exact linear certificates.
keywords: set covering weighted cover resource capacity upper bound nonnegative coverage
topics.inputs: Selected original resource rows, target expression, explicit multipliers and any required variable bounds.
topics.guarantees: check.linear checks the actual coefficients and residual bounds, including overlaps and variables outside the target support.
topics.non_guarantees: There is no minimum set-cover solver or automatic cover-cut generator. Support coverage alone is not a linear proof.
topics.body:
Build membership from original terms with set=row and member=var. Use ops.sets.pairs and ops.sets.members for containment, overlap and uncovered members.
Choose a cover and its multipliers explicitly or with an external algorithm. Verify target <= U with check.linear and residual="bounds" when original bounds control the coefficient residual.
For many targets, use check.linear_many. A smaller cover is a candidate improvement, not evidence until verification succeeds.
For closure-union consumption, use recipe.closure; that is distinct from choosing resource rows to cover a target.
Cover inequalities for a knapsack need their own integer-valid certificate; they do not follow from set membership alone.

topics.title: Graph matching algorithms are not provided
topics.summary: Matching edges with disjoint endpoints is a different task from graph isomorphism or table joins.
keywords: maximum cardinality weighted matching disjoint edges unmatched vertices
topics.non_guarantees: No maximum-cardinality or weighted matching solver is provided. A chosen matching is not a proof of optimality or a MIP inequality.
topics.body:
Construct a candidate matching externally and check that its edges exist and its endpoints are disjoint using Frames.
If selected edges encode proved inequalities, combine their original source sides with check.linear to verify an explicit target bound.
Use alg.graph.isomorphism_classes only for label-preserving bijections between graph instances, not for disjoint-edge selection.

topics.title: Check fractional point feasibility in the relaxation
topics.summary: Use exact matrix activity and bound comparisons to inspect an LP relaxation point.
keywords: fractional solution feasible relaxation witness rational point row variable bounds
topics.inputs: A complete exact Frame(var,value), uniquely keyed by var and bound to the model snapshot.
topics.guarantees: m.matrix.activity computes exact row activities; compare both row sides and all variable bounds explicitly.
topics.non_guarantees: check.solution checks the integer model and rejects domain="relaxation". Fractional values on integer variables fail its integrality check.
topics.body:
Use m.matrix.activity(values), with the default missing="error", then join the result to m.rows on row and compare activity against lb and ub.
Independently check full variable coverage and both variable bounds, including variables absent from every row.
A point that passes these comparisons is feasible for the linear relaxation; it need not satisfy integrality.
LinExpr.evaluate only evaluates one expression; it is not a feasibility check. A feasible point is not an optimality or implication certificate.
Use check.solution for a complete point that must also satisfy the original integer domains.

topics.title: Report resource lifecycle
topics.summary: Mathematical Reports share paged certificate storage; evidence views and proof dependencies retain the data they need.
keywords: report resources file descriptor exhaustion cleanup close memory batch certificates
topics.guarantees: Scalar mathematical checkers release their temporary workspace after publication and share retained evidence per live model owner. Batch targets share one store; for_target does not open another database.
topics.non_guarantees: Report and LinExpr have no public close() method. Retained evidence still uses memory and disk. Unrelated queries and separately retained batches have their own storage; memory_mb is not a global process budget.
topics.body:
Use check.linear_batch() for a loop of explicit claims, sources and per-target assumptions. Use check.linear_many when the inputs already exist as Frames.
Retaining thousands of scalar mathematical Reports does not allocate one persistent SQLite connection per Report. Releasing the last Report, Claim, evidence Frame and dependent proof for a node makes its stored rows reclaimable; free database pages can be reused.
Small expressions use bounded exact in-memory terms; larger materialized expressions share spill storage. Temporary SQLite callbacks do not keep discarded workspaces alive; manual garbage collection is not part of the API contract.
Keep source models and proof dependencies alive until verification and any Edit that consumes them are complete.
Export needed audit data with Report.to_spec or Report.write; exported status alone is not a live proof and must be replayed before reuse.
Release unneeded reports, evidence Frames, expressions and containers holding them. Dependent reports and staged edits may still retain references, so deleting one name need not free storage immediately.
Model.close releases owned query resources and invalidates dependent live results. Close a model only when its live results are no longer needed.
Do not call private report stores to close shared evidence. This release offers no per-report deterministic close API.

topics.title: Exact arithmetic and external numerical values
topics.summary: Use integer, Fraction, finite Decimal or mf.q text for mathematical scalars.
topics.guarantees: m.check and LinExpr operate on the exact rational values of the bound snapshot.
topics.non_guarantees: Converting a solver float to a rational does not certify feasibility, optimality or a dual bound.
topics.body:
Booleans, NaN, infinity and Python floats are rejected as algebraic scalars. Infinity is allowed in Frame number columns representing bounds.
Frame arithmetic keeps finite quotients exact, including finite/infinity = Fraction(0). Indeterminate infinity arithmetic (infinity-infinity, zero*infinity, infinity/infinity and sums of opposite infinities) raises ExactArithmeticError.
If an external approximate value is useful for candidate ranking, explicitly choose and record its conversion outside mipframe.
For proof multipliers, replay the resulting rational certificate including residual bound compensation.
Exact solution checking may reject a rounded solver point. Do not silently add a tolerance or label it exact.
SciPy export is an explicit float64 conversion; overflow, nonfinite results and nonzero underflow are errors.

topics.title: Execution budgets and bounded display
topics.summary: Preview size, materialization size, algorithm output and search completeness are different limits.
topics.guarantees: Complete ops finish or raise; no truncated mathematical result is returned.
topics.non_guarantees: head() cannot bypass a join validation barrier, sort or aggregation. repr does not promise constant-time upstream work.
topics.body:
Working memory defaults to 128 MiB (minimum 16 KiB). Disk spill is exact; the budget is not a process RSS limit. Parsing has a separate 32 MiB minimum.
to_records explicitly materialize and can raise MaterializationLimitError; use iter_batches/write for large outputs.
Most ops default to 1,000,000 output records. Set max_output_rows=None only when full output is intended.
alg *_candidates may stop early and record scope/stop reason. Exhaustive algorithms raise SearchBudgetExceeded when incomplete.
check.enumerate returns INCONCLUSIVE when its enumeration budget is exhausted; this is different from alg.integer.enumerate.
MatrixView repr reports statistics without dense conversion. preview defaults to an 8 by 12 grid, independent of global display options.

topics.title: Candidate search versus exhaustive algorithms
topics.summary: Use alg for potentially expensive searches; inspect its declared domain and completeness.
topics.guarantees: Candidates are verified graph objects in the selected graph. Exhaustive searches either finish or raise.
topics.non_guarantees: A top-k candidate ranking is not a global optimum or a MIP cut proof.
topics.body:
clique_candidates and odd_cycle_candidates return ordinary Frames with normalized membership and search information in relations.
maximal_cliques means inclusion-maximal, not maximum-cardinality. simple_cycles and isomorphism_classes are explicit exhaustive searches.
vertices declares the graph domain; scope induces the search subgraph. Do not pass a subset as the full domain while retaining out-of-domain edges.
Structural isomorphism only respects the supplied graph labels; it does not prove an automorphism of the whole optimization model.

topics.title: Recover from a failed query
topics.summary: Read the original error and its complete report, then query its linked help topic.
topics.guarantees: Suggestions name real current APIs; exceptions retain their original types and evidence.
topics.non_guarantees: A resource error or malformed input is not a mathematical counterexample.
topics.body:
Use mf.help(exc) inside an exception handler. If exc.report exists, inspect its summary and pageable violations.
Do not fix a strict projection by taking the first neighbor. Inspect zero/multiple matches or refine the target selection explicitly.
Do not silence cardinality errors with m:m unless that relationship is intended. Do not bypass proof errors by omitting because and claiming equivalence.

topics.title: Join uniqueness and complete matching
topics.summary: Join cardinality and match coverage are separate contracts.
topics.guarantees: Explicit 1:1, 1:m or m:1 validates the required uniqueness over the entire input.
topics.non_guarantees: Unknown uniqueness does not mean duplicates were found. select("var") on Terms does not make var unique.
topics.example: Q = A.join(B, on="var", cardinality="1:1", require="left")
topics.body:
auto needs an existing uniqueness fact on at least one side. Otherwise specify the intended cardinality explicitly.
Use m:m only for an intended expansion. require=left/right/both verifies complete matching independently.
Rename conflicting non-key fields with select; there are no implicit suffixes. head(1) cannot suppress invalid later input.
A failed check retains all duplicate or unmatched records in its report.

topics.title: Navigate entities and terms explicitly
topics.summary: Coefficients belong to Terms, not Row or Var entities.
topics.guarantees: one() requires exactly one item; it never silently selects a representative.
topics.non_guarantees: Neighborhood .rows/.vars forgets source-to-target edge multiplicity.
topics.example:
term = x.terms.where(row=R).one()
term.row, term.var, term.coef
topics.body:
Replace Frame [] with iloc, loc, family, where or column according to intent. Entity selections expose ids.
Use rows.loc[ref] for Ref[row] and vars.loc[ref] for Ref[var] with matching uid/version. A Ref outside the selection raises KeyError.
Use ref.bind(model) to navigate the full matching snapshot; do not strip .id to bypass an axis or snapshot mismatch.
Use V.project(...) directly for source-preserving strict adjacency projection.
Use m.matrix.nnz(rows=R, vars=V, axis="var") for zero-aware participation counts.
Terms are the unified edge view; exported to_records() is the explicit mutable-record exit.

topics.title: Table predicates and affine model expressions
topics.summary: QueryExpr selects table records; LinExpr describes an affine function of model variables.
topics.guarantees: Query predicates use &, | and ~. Mathematical inequalities use s <= U or s >= L, also LinExpr.le(U) or LinExpr.ge(L). Equalities use .eq().
topics.non_guarantees: x == y is entity identity, not a linear equation. Claim and Report have no implicit truth value.
topics.example:
T = m.terms().where((mf.col("coef") < 0) & mf.col("var").isin(V))
claim = (2*x - y).eq(0)
topics.body:
Core Frame predicates do not accept arbitrary Python callbacks. Use col to form serializable expressions.
Inspect report.status or call require(). Constructing a Claim does not add a row or prove it.

topics.title: Template similarity is not full model symmetry
topics.summary: Graph or template equality does not prove a permutation preserves the whole MIP.
keywords: symmetry
automorphism
isomorphism
topics.non_guarantees: Graph or template equality does not prove a permutation preserves the whole MIP.
topics.body: A full claim must account for every coefficient, row bound, variable bound, domain, objective and external coupling under an explicit bijection. No general MIP symmetry checker or symmetry-breaking certificate is provided.

topics.title: General disjunction certificates are not available
topics.summary: One-hot epigraph strengthening may require reasoning outside the current checkers.
keywords: one hot
epigraph
disjunctive
convex hull
peak
topics.non_guarantees: One-hot epigraph strengthening may require reasoning outside the current checkers.
topics.body: Frame queries can validate the one-hot rows and assemble branch data. check.cases combines same-target proofs over one finite model-integer variable, retaining other assumptions. There is no general continuous disjunction merger or infeasible-branch elimination rule. Do not fabricate a PROVED Report.

topics.title: Optimization and presolve are external
topics.summary: mipframe inspects and verifies snapshots; it does not solve or provide a presolve/postsolve mapping.
keywords: solver
optimality
solve
presolve
postsolve
topics.non_guarantees: mipframe inspects and verifies snapshots; it does not solve or provide a presolve/postsolve mapping.
topics.body: Use an external solver for candidate points, multipliers and optimization. Bind any returned data to the actual snapshot. check.solution establishes feasibility and an objective value, not optimality. Solver statuses and tolerances are external evidence.

topics.title: Exact native and LP output
topics.summary: Native save is lossless; LP output has explicit representability restrictions.
keywords: MPS write
write_mps
export mps
free row
roundtrip
topics.non_guarantees: Native save is lossless; LP output has explicit representability restrictions.
topics.body: There is no MPS writer. LP export rejects nonterminating decimal rationals and unrepresentable free rows rather than changing mathematics. Use native save for lossless persistence and audit.roundtrip for supported LP files.

topics.title: Dropping a variable is not elimination
topics.summary: Edit.drop_vars only removes variables absent from all final rows and the final objective.
keywords: elimination
substitution
quotient
reformulation
topics.non_guarantees: Edit.drop_vars only removes variables absent from all final rows and the final objective.
topics.body: LinExpr.substitute is algebra without proof. Edit does not provide automatic variable elimination, quotient reformulation, Model.from_frames or projection equivalence for changed coordinates.

keywords: claim construction inequality equality comparison operators affine proposition
topics.when: Construct an unproved affine proposition with <=, >=, LinExpr.le/ge or .eq().
topics.inputs: Model variables or a LinExpr and an exact scalar or compatible affine expression.
topics.returns: Claim; constructing it neither proves it nor adds a row.
topics.non_guarantees: Python == is not mathematical equality for model entities. A newly constructed Claim is not a trusted original source side.
topics.example:
expr = 2*x - y
upper = expr <= 3
lower = expr >= 0
equality = expr.eq(1)
topics.body:
Build expressions from variable arithmetic, row.expr or m.linexpr. Use mf.q("1/2") for fractional scalars.
Create target inequalities with <= or >= and equalities with .eq(); Claim and Report have no implicit truth value.
LinExpr.le(U) and LinExpr.ge(L) are equivalent method forms of <= and >=.
For trusted sources use row.lb_claim, row.ub_claim, var.lb_claim or var.ub_claim, or a compatible proved Report.
Verify a target with m.check before passing its proof to an Edit. Direct Claim constructor arguments are not the expression-building interface.

topics.title: Checker.cases
topics.summary: Discharge an exhaustive finite integer split over one variable.
topics.when: Discharge an exhaustive finite integer split over one variable.
topics.inputs: Exact claims, original source sides or previously verified Reports; see signature.
topics.returns: Report with complete scope, dependencies and evidence.
topics.guarantees: Every branch proves the same exact target; only its matching equality assumption is removed. Remaining assumptions are unioned. The result is integer-only.
topics.non_guarantees: No solver call, multiplier search, automatic condition discharge or model edit.
topics.failures: Invalid sources, missing input, bad multipliers, cross-snapshot input or unsupported domains raise; they are not INCONCLUSIVE.
topics.resources: Working memory defaults to 128 MiB (minimum 16 KiB). Disk spill is exact; the budget is not a process RSS limit.
topics.body:
var is a same-snapshot Var or VarRef with integer kind and finite model bounds. cases maps exact integer values to verified exact PROVED Reports with the same target relation, constant and coefficients.
Keys must exactly cover ceil(lb)..floor(ub); duplicates after normalization, empty domains, floats and booleans are rejected. Coverage never uses branch assumptions.
Each branch must assume a*y+b==0 for this variable and value. Remove matching equalities only; preserve the union of every other explicit or inherited assumption. Nested calls can discharge multiple variables.
domain="auto" and "integer" produce integer proofs; "relaxation" is rejected. Missing/invalid branches raise, not REFUTED. Infeasible Reports cannot substitute for target proofs.
Use ordinary linear checks to align stronger or differently scaled conclusions first. Branches may contain continuous variables. Results support Edit.because only when no assumptions remain; all model fact dependencies and integer-domain coverage bounds remain auditable.
The cases and discharged evidence Frames record branch parent indices and removed assumptions. Replay rechecks all branches and coverage.

topics.title: Checker.linear_batch
topics.summary: Build a batch of linear certificates with scalar arguments and per-target assumptions.
aliases: check many linear certificates at once
keywords: batch linear certificates bulk scalar claims assume assumptions branch proofs simple builder
topics.when: Build a batch of linear certificates with scalar arguments and per-target assumptions.
topics.inputs: residual="exact" or "bounds"; domain="auto", "relaxation" or "integer"; memory_mb and disk_mb apply to the whole batch.
topics.returns: LinearBatch context manager. add stages each check; run verifies all targets and returns a Report.
topics.guarantees: Consumes inputs incrementally in shared storage. No caller-authored schemas or reports mapping are required.
topics.non_guarantees: No multiplier search, condition discharge, enumeration batch or model edit.
topics.failures: Unsupported methods or options raise. Invalid inputs, cancellation and resource failures abort unpublished work.
topics.resources: Working memory defaults to 128 MiB (minimum 16 KiB). Disk spill is exact; the budget is not a process RSS limit.
topics.example:
with m.check.linear_batch(residual="bounds") as batch:
    for row in m.rows:
        batch.add(key=str(row.id), target=row.ub_claim, using=[row.ub_claim])
    report = batch.run()
report.require()
topics.body:
The example requires finite upper bounds on the selected rows. Replace targets and sources with the actual propositions and certificates to verify.
Prefer this builder for ordinary Python loops. If targets/terms/using are already Frames, use linear_many instead.
The returned report remains usable after leaving the with block. Use report.for_target(key) for one conclusion, including its explicit and inherited assumptions.

keywords: Inspect structural roles and raw coefficients

topics.when: A signature suggests repeated rows, but coefficients may vary.
topics.inputs: m is open; R is an explicitly selected RowFrame.
topics.guarantees: Actual observed coefficient statistics of the selected rows.
topics.non_guarantees: A family label is not an original formula, and observations do not prove a semantic role.
topics.example:
ir = m.ir
T = m.terms(rows=R)
G = T.group_by("row").agg(
    distinct=mf.col("coef").nunique(),
    amin=mf.col("coef").min(), amax=mf.col("coef").max(),
)
G.head()
topics.body:
## When to use
A signature suggests repeated rows, but coefficients may vary.
Inputs: m is open; R is an explicitly selected RowFrame.

## Primitive pattern
IR / signature → selected Terms → exact grouped coefficient statistics.

## Minimal code
```python
ir = m.ir
T = m.terms(rows=R)
G = T.group_by("row").agg(
    distinct=mf.col("coef").nunique(),
    amin=mf.col("coef").min(), amax=mf.col("coef").max(),
)
G.head()
```

## What it establishes
Actual observed coefficient statistics of the selected rows.

## What it does not establish

I.tensors, I.operators, I.partitions and I.evidence are ordinary Frames.

---
name: mipframe
description: Inspect linear LP/MPS models with mipframe, compose exact sparse queries, verify explicit claims, and build independent edited snapshots. Use for model analysis and verified transformations, not as an optimization solver.
---

# Working with mipframe

This guide targets MIPFrame 1.0.0 and Python 3.11 or newer. Check the configured interpreter and `mf.__version__`.
If the installed version matches this skill, use the current interpreter.
Do not search for or switch to another Python environment.

```python
import sys
import mipframe as mf
print(sys.executable, sys.version)
print(mf.__version__)
mf.help()
```

MIPFrame represents a linear MIP as immutable rows, variables, sparse terms and
model metadata. Compressed IR suggests structural hypotheses. Frames and `mf.ops`
compute exact structural facts. `mf.alg` searches graph or finite integer objects.
`LinExpr`, `Claim` and `m.check` express and verify mathematical propositions.
An `Edit` builds a different snapshot; it never mutates its source.

## Find the capability before inventing syntax

Query `mf.help("recover coordinates")`, `mf.help("linear certificate")`, or another
English task description. An exact public name such as `mf.help("VarFrame.project")`
opens its contract. `mf.help(mf.ops.sets.pairs)` accepts actual registered callables.
Read a full topic with `detail="full"`; use `format="json"` for structured results.
The same documentation is available through `python -m mipframe help "query"`.
Search is local, versioned and deterministic. It does not execute an analysis.

Start from these six actions:

- Observe: `m.ir`, `m.rows`, `m.vars`, family summaries and bounded examples.
- Navigate: `.rows` and `.vars` for entities, `.terms` for original coefficients.
- Relate: Frame filters, joins, grouping and strict coordinate projection.
- Compute or search: exact sets/graphs/matrix operations, then explicit alg searches.
- Verify: an explicit Claim and the appropriate checker, including its scope.
- Modify: stage an Edit, inspect its summary, build and audit the new snapshot.

Do not guess methods such as `detect_network`, `find_symmetry`, `auto_reformulate`
or `write_mps`. Search the intended capability; a limitation topic may be the
correct answer. Inspect a public signature or docstring when the argument contract
is uncertain. Avoid rebuilding parsers or sparse indexing already supplied by the
library, while keeping ordinary Python available for small custom calculations.

## Unified entity and indexed navigation

Use `m.vars` / `m.rows`, `by_name(name)`, `loc[id_or_ref]`, and `iloc[position]`.
Bounds are exact finite values or infinities; `source_line` is one-based or `None`.
`to_records()` explicitly materializes detached records within a budget.
Export a numerical SciPy copy with `m.matrix.view().to_scipy()`.

Indexed directories follow the family Frame model: `I = m.indexed()`, then
`O = I.operators.where(...)`, `O.rows`, and `O.related("kernel")` or
`O.related("bindings")`. `I.operator(id)` returns a one-row Frame, so metadata
uses `O.one().row_count` or `O.one().formula`. Tensor members use `T.vars`;
its axes use `T.related("axes").where(axis=0).rows`. Frame.shape is the table
shape; indexed dimensions are in `related("dimensions")`.
Keep `indexed_key` when projecting to preserve related navigation. All relations
follow the current selection and share storage. Use `inspect(max_items=...)` for
bounded previews, including ordinary Frames. Indexed views additionally support
`verbose`; family-specific display options are rejected on other providers.

`m.verify()` and `I.verify(selection)` return Reports with integrity/indexed scope.
Inconsistency returns REFUTED; use `.require()` to raise. Neither is a linear
certificate or an Edit justification. `summary["checked"]` and `summary["failures"]`
count primary checks; `evidence["checks"]` lists these checks and
`evidence["details"]` adds subordinate diagnostics. A skipped or inconclusive check
prevents an overall PROVED result. Use mathematical checkers for those claims.
All mathematical checkers use exact arithmetic; no tolerance or arithmetic switch
changes their comparison rules. See `mf.help("concept.indexed", detail="full")`.

## Observe, hypothesize, query, verify, act, audit

Read the IR after importing a model. `read()` and `load()` prepare default IR and
indexed results before returning, so loading is real work. Displaying IR does not
start a second search. Use samples to choose hypotheses and full declared scopes
to establish them. A small example is not a proof about every family member.

```python
m = mf.read("model.mps")
m.ir
m.rows.head()
mf.help("recipe.coordinates", detail="full")
```

Keep explanations separate from verified facts. Anonymous coefficients can support
a precise statement about incidence without identifying the original application.
Names may suggest a useful coordinate map, but the map still requires coverage,
uniqueness and numerical checks. Family labels belong to a snapshot, configuration
and refinement depth; their numbers are not portable across models or versions.

Structural signatures are normalized observations, not original formulas. Inspect
original terms and bounds before reasoning about a row. Equal support does not
imply equal coefficients, equal bounds, redundancy or symmetry. Comparing complete
local templates still omits any external coupling that was not in the payload.

## Structural families

Start with `m.row_families` or `m.var_families`: both are template structural
Frames at depth 2. `m.family("F0")` is a one-row Frame with `.rows`; variable
families have `.vars`. Filter several families and use the same navigation.
`m.rows.head(100).families()` restricts members, preserving global family IDs.
`count` is selected coverage; `total_count` is the full-model population.

Use `f.related("pattern")` for exact structural tokens, `f.related("parameters")`
for numeric summaries, and `f.related("histogram")` for complete distributions.
Filter `basis="canonical"`, `"raw"` or `"scale_normalized"` explicitly; retain
`orientation` when comparing zero-RHS equalities. `f.inspect()` is bounded.
Keep `family_key` when selecting columns if you need later relation navigation.
A depth-d row pattern references depth-(d-1) variable roles, not necessarily the
families in the default variable directory.

Advanced algebraic, typed and exact structural rules live in
`mf.analysis.families/signatures(..., method=...)`, always returning Frames.
Use `m.refinement(...)` for parent/child transitions and `m.indexed(...)` for
indexed discovery. There is no `m.structure` or public Family/Signature object.

## Rows, Vars, Terms and identity

The canonical tables are Rows `(row,name,lb,ub)`, Vars
`(var,name,kind,lb,ub,obj,source_line)` and Terms `(row,var,coef)`. Finite numeric facts are
exact rationals. Terms exclude the objective, bounds and structural zeros.
Canonical variable kind is C or I; binary status is derived from effective integer
bounds and includes variables fixed at zero or one.

Use `m.rows.iloc[0]` for a position, `.loc[key]` for a declared key,
`.by_name("name")` for explicit name lookup. Use `m.family("F0@2").rows`
or `m.family("V0@2").vars` for family members. Frame `[]` is not a mixed-purpose index.
Use `.ids` for original IDs and typed Ref columns for relationships.
`m.rows.loc[ref]` and `m.vars.loc[ref]` accept typed Refs with matching snapshot
uid/version and entity axis, and require membership in the selected Frame.
`ref.bind(m)` navigates the full matching model. `.loc[ref.id]` uses only the
integer ID and cannot validate the Ref's snapshot or axis; prefer `.loc[ref]`.

`r.vars` and `x.rows` are deduplicated entity sets. A coefficient belongs to
`r.terms` or `x.terms`; `term.row` and `term.var` navigate its endpoints.
`one()` requires exactly one output, never an arbitrary representative.

```python
x = m.vars.iloc[0]
term = x.terms.head(1).one()  # requires a nonzero column
term.row, term.var, term.coef
```

Independent imports have different snapshot identities. Save/load preserves uid
and version. Same spelling does not authorize cross-model joins. Presolved names
do not supply a postsolve map. Keep every model referenced by a live result open;
export detached records if data must outlive it. New Edit snapshots are independent
but Diff and proof navigation can still depend on the parent remaining open.

## Compose relations with explicit contracts

Use `mf.col` for serializable table expressions, `&`, `|`, `~` for predicates.
Do not use Python `and/or` or lambda callbacks in the core query language.
`select` and `join` return ordinary Frames; filtering and slicing retain entity
type. Direct key retention can preserve uniqueness; choosing a non-key column
cannot create it. `Terms.select("var")` is usually not unique.

For joins, specify the intended cardinality when existing facts do not establish
it. `cardinality="1:1"` and `require="left"` are separate requests: the first
checks uniqueness, the second checks coverage. Unknown uniqueness is not a finding
of duplicates. Use `m:m` only for an intended expansion. Rename conflicting fields
explicitly with select. `head(1)` cannot bypass whole-input validation.

A strict `V.project(i=A,j=B)` requires one adjacent target in each domain for every
source variable. Then `P.check("product", ("i","j")).require()` checks the full
declared Cartesian product. Filtering or head does not shrink those target domains.
Inspect complete violations on zero/multiple matches instead of choosing the first.
For participation counts including isolated members use `m.matrix.nnz`; ordinary
Terms group-by emits observed groups only.

## Choose exact computation or candidate search

Use sets.pairs/members for support relationships and witnesses; sets.components for
hypergraph blocks; graph reachability for directed closure. Closure union resource
sums must count shared members once: use sets.pair_aggregate. A directed path is a
graph witness; deletion of its corresponding model rows still requires a linear
certificate from retained row sides.

`mf.ops` completes or raises. `mf.alg` distinguishes candidate APIs from exhaustive
searches. Read the search metadata and selected scope. A greedy top-k clique search
does not prove a maximum clique. Graph cliques and odd cycles do not prove that the
original MIP edges are conflicts. Supply and check those sources independently.

Use `MatrixView.preview()` only when a small grid helps. The default is 8 by 12;
most_active ranks columns over all selected rows, not just the row prefix.
`to_scipy()` explicitly converts to independent float64 CSR. Exact reasoning stays
on the rational path; conversion can fail on overflow or nonzero underflow.

## Verify mathematical statements

Use `row.expr` for raw coefficients, not for row bounds. Use `row.lb_claim`,
`row.ub_claim`, `row.eq_claim` or variable bound claims as original fact sources.
`x == y` compares entity identities; `.eq()` constructs a mathematical equality.
For inequalities use `s <= U` or `s >= L`; `LinExpr.le(U)` and `LinExpr.ge(L)`
are equivalent method forms. Constructing a Claim neither proves it nor adds a row.
Claims and Reports have no implicit bool. Check `status` or call `require()`.

Use `mf.q("9.6")` or `mf.q("43/39")`, not a Python float. Converting approximate
solver multipliers to rationals is only a proposal; replay the full certificate
with residual bound compensation. Exactness is relative to this saved snapshot,
not an unknown pre-presolve model or unsaved original token spelling.

`identity` checks algebra; `linear` checks supplied multipliers; `infeasible`
checks contradiction; `round` uses integer-valued expressions; `enumerate` checks
a finite local integer implication; `solution` validates a complete exact point
against the mathematical integer model, including integrality. It rejects
`domain="relaxation"`. For a fractional LP point use `m.matrix.activity(values)`
plus exact checks of both row sides and every variable bound. Check complete
variable coverage, including variables absent from all rows; activity alone only
requires participating variables. See `mf.help("fractional point feasibility")`.
No checker searches for multipliers.

For many linear checks, use the scalar-style batch builder. It accepts the same
`using` and `assume` arguments as `linear`, without constructing schemas:

```python
with m.check.linear_batch(residual="bounds") as batch:
    for key, claim, sources, assumptions in checks:
        batch.add(key=key, target=claim, using=sources, assume=assumptions)
    report = batch.run()
report.require()
proof = report.for_target(key)
```

Keys are unique nonempty strings. `add` consumes each input immediately; `run`
verifies and publishes the complete batch. Results survive the builder's context
exit. Every target retains its own explicit and inherited assumptions; a batch
does not merge branches or discharge conditions. If targets, terms and sources
already exist as Frames, use `linear_many`. See `mf.help("Checker.linear_batch")`.

An insufficient certificate is INCONCLUSIVE, not a proof that the target is false.
A local enumeration counterexample need not extend to a full-model feasible point.
A feasible point does not prove optimality. Integer-only evidence cannot prove an
LP claim. Assumptions remain in the report, including those inherited from parents.
Use `m.check.cases(target, var=y, cases={0:p0, 1:p1})` to explicitly discharge
an exhaustive split over a finite model-integer variable. Each branch must prove
the same target and assume its matching value. Only those equalities disappear;
other assumptions remain. The result is integer-only and supports `because`
only when unconditional. Branches may involve continuous activity variables.
A contradiction under z=1 does not automatically discharge the condition to create
an unconditional z=0 certificate. General continuous disjunction merging and full
MIP symmetry certification are not implemented.

## Modify and audit deliberately

Stage edits against one source snapshot. Setters use exact scalars or key-aligned
Frames, not positional arrays. Omitted bounds preserve the old side; None is not
infinity. Changing coefficients requires a new row identity. Dropping a variable
requires no final row or objective references; it is not variable elimination.

An omitted because permits an unverified modification without asserting equivalence.
A supplied because is strict: proved, exact, unconditional, matching source and
covering the modification. Deletion proofs must close to retained facts; self-proof
and ungrounded cycles fail. New rows become usable premises only after an
intermediate build and a new check on that snapshot.
For a case-proved replacement, first add the new row with `because`, build,
then prove and delete the old row on the new snapshot. Check both direct-parent
Diffs; comparing across multiple edits is not supported.

Inspect separate LP/MIP semantics and objective relations in Diff. A valid cut need
not improve an LP objective or solver time. Native save is lossless; LP export rejects
unrepresentable exact data. `mf.audit.roundtrip` checks supported LP serialization,
not mathematical implication. There is no MPS writer or automatic elimination.

## Recover and control output

When a call fails, inspect its original diagnostics and complete pageable report.
Use `mf.help(exc)` or its help_topic to find a correction. Do not discard violations
or weaken a contract merely to continue with an unsupported conclusion.

Avoid full record dumps. repr is bounded but upstream joins, sorts or aggregations
can still require complete work. Query memory defaults to 128 MiB with a 16 KiB
minimum; parsing has a separate 32 MiB minimum. Budgets do not bound process RSS.
Use iter_batches/write for large exports. Output limits fail complete ops rather
than silently truncating them. Search and enumeration budget statuses have different
contracts; consult their exact topics.

Scalar mathematical Reports share retained certificate storage; keeping thousands
does not require one persistent database connection per proof. Small expressions
use bounded exact memory and larger expressions share spill storage. Evidence
Frames, Claims, dependent Reports and Edits keep the data they still need alive.
Release unneeded containers to reclaim that data; routine `gc.collect()` is not
required. Export replayable certificates with `Report.write` or `to_spec` when
they must outlive the model. `Model.close` invalidates live dependent results.
There is no public `Report.close` or `LinExpr.close`; see
`mf.help("concept.report-resources")` for ownership and resource scope.

Use an external solver for optimization and an explicit mapping for solver data.
Use source text when provenance or serialization itself is the question. The goal
is a justified result with its actual scope, not forcing every computation into a
mipframe primitive or inferring domain semantics from an attractive pattern.
